property_summary: After any call to setOwner, the new owner must equal the _owner argument supplied; the buggy version sets any caller's supplied _owner, while the reference version reverts for non-admin callers, so the bug violates the invariant for non-admin callers.
For any address that is not the original admin, calling setOwner(_owner) must revert; the buggy version allows it to succeed and change the owner.

For any caller authorized as admin, after setOwner(_owner) succeeds, the owner state variable must equal the _owner argument passed; the buggy version breaks this by always setting owner to a hardcoded address instead.

For any caller, calling setOwner(_owner) must only succeed when the caller is the admin; the bug lets the current owner also change the owner, so after an owner's call to setOwner(newOwner), P.owner() remains unchanged while M.owner() becomes newOwner.
Any non-admin caller must fail to change the owner via setOwner; the buggy modifier allows any caller to succeed.

Only the original admin should be able to change the owner; the buggy modifier lets any caller change the owner, so after setOwner is called by a non-admin, the owner state variable differs between the reference and the mutant.

For any caller and any address argument, after setOwner is called, the new owner equals the caller if the caller is the admin, and equals the previous owner otherwise; the buggy version sets the owner to the argument even when the caller is not the admin.
For any non-reverting call to setOwner, the return value must be true; the bug version returns false, violating this invariant.
After a successful setOwner call, the contract's owner variable must equal the address passed; the bug still updates owner but returns false.

In reference C, after any successful `setOwner` call (i.e. one that does not revert), the return value must equal its internal success value that is always true; the mutant can return false on success instead, violating that the return value equals the stored intent.

The reference implementation always returns true from setOwner when called by the admin; the buggy version always reverts, violating the invariant that setOwner never reverts when called by the admin.
For any admin caller, setOwner always returns true in the reference but returns false in the mutant because the return statement was deleted.
For any call to setOwner by an admin, the reference implementation always returns true; the mutant omits the return statement, so the function returns the default false.
For any admin caller, setOwner should set the owner to the provided _owner address; the buggy version always sets it to address(0), violating the rule.
After setOwner is called by the admin, the owner state variable must equal the address passed to setOwner; the bug causes owner to stay unchanged instead.

The reference contract C only allows the admin (deployer) to change the owner via setOwner; the buggy version allows any caller to change the owner. This can be observed by checking that the owner only changes when called by admin in the reference, but may change for a non-admin in the buggy version.

After any call to setOwner, if the caller is not the admin, the owner state variable must remain unchanged in the reference; the buggy version violates this by allowing a non-admin to change the owner.

For any non-admin caller, a call to setOwner(_newOwner) must revert and leave the owner unchanged in the reference; the buggy version allows a non-admin to successfully change the owner without reverting.
